These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. rec4Z2QI5tKVlLiOw.Bio: Juan Ayala hosts "The Juan On Juan Podcast," covering conspiratorial and occult topics, and appeared on InnerVerse discussing Gnostic archons/overlords and the alchemical mystery of the homunculus.
rec4Z2QI5tKVlLiOw.Name: Juan Ayala

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

recZOKCUcQhghoKqF.Bio: Kayleigh Berkana is an astrologer who has appeared as a recurring panelist on InnerVerse group discussions (alongside Slick Dissident, Mario Garza, and others) covering topics like Lovecraftian mythology, Jack Parsons, and occult symbolism.
recZOKCUcQhghoKqF.Name: Kayleigh Berkana

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Parsons as mystic first, scientist second", "body": "Juan Ayala frames Jack Parsons as a mystic before a rocket scientist: a man who never graduated yet innovated rocketry when it was still considered science fiction, much as Juan says Descartes drew ideas from dreams. Juan traces the family back to the Witch of Northampton, then follows Parsons into the Agape Lodge of the OTO near his home, his father and son bond with Crowley, and the Babalon Working with L. Ron Hubbard in the desert. He argues Parsons wanted real results from magic the way he got them from explosives, and lists the competing theories of his death, from a fire elemental to homunculus work to murder."}, {"title": "Fiction as a tool on the world mind", "body": "Chance Garton argues that Parsons, Crowley, Lovecraft and Hubbard formed an alchemical inversion aimed at the world mind, getting people to act out a fantasy until parts of it come true. The panel chases that idea through popular culture: Juan's claim that Tony Stark's father is modeled on Parsons' father, with Marvel later tying Stark to Mephisto; Chance's reading of Jonathan Hickman's comic East of West, with a child named Babylon and an AI called Balloon; and a Punisher plot Chance says makes a real conspiracy look fictional. Juan adds that a script Parsons wrote with Frank Malina had its hero blow himself up years before Parsons did."}, {"title": "Sevens, Babalon and the Silver Star", "body": "Mario Garza follows the number seven through the story: Juan's account of an entity telling Parsons something would unfold if he lived seven more years, the call of the seventh aether recited in the Babalon Working, and the seven-pointed star of Crowley's Silver Star order with Babalon written in its points. Sharing Lon Milo DuQuette's tarot cards and the short film The Wormwood Star about Marjorie Cameron, Mario links that star to the Lust card, where Babalon rides the seven-headed beast. The panel also notes the respelling of Babylon as Babalon for gematria, which one guest hears as balloon, a word he ties to official UFO explanations."}, {"title": "Reading Jack Parsons through astrology", "body": "Kayleigh Berkana reads the story astrologically, starting with the Mars and Saturn conjunction she finds in the sky when the Babalon Working began, a pairing she associates with blow-ups. In Parsons' chart she points to two grand water trines, which she reads as deep psychic sensitivity, and Saturn conjunct Pluto in Cancer in his first house, which she ties to issues with authority and father figures. She calls scientism dark side Aquarius, reads his Jupiter and Uranus in Aquarius as a scientific legacy, and places Lilith in his twelfth house. Juan, who says he does not really believe in astrology, concedes the father figure reading fits."}, {"title": "Scientism as a modern seance", "body": "Chance argues that scientism is only presented as materialist in public, while the science with lasting impact is alchemical. Slick Dissident answers with seancism: science as a seance that evokes the names of long dead men of renown, like Einstein, to claim the power to predict outcomes, which he calls necromantic. Another panelist calls scientism a heliocentric program of anti-spirituality that teaches how far away Mars is but never what it means. Mario Garza goes further, calling science fiction mostly propaganda and saying the moon landing looks like science fiction to him, while Juan suggests the alchemists' elixir of eternal life is living on in people's minds."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Worlds will collide tonight as the Spider-Verse dream team convenes for a magical livestream about the strange secrets & occult occurrences connecting Jack Parsons of JPL, Crowley, dark occult rituals, the founding of NASA, and much more. With mystic perspectives from Slick Dissident, symbolic syncretism from Mario Garza, astrological evidence from Kayleigh Berkana, and the jovial rabbit holes Juan Ayala has been digging, this promises to be an extravagant exploration.

Positive side Aquarius is like decentralized groups and actually making humanitarian adjustments for the world.", "author": "Kayleigh Berkana", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/5c923247-58f8-42f0-a64e-59357e5336f4/KAYLEIGH-BERKANA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The fiction, the way it's wielded, is not just to get people to believe in things that aren't real but also to make them not believe things that are real.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I feel like I had a better grasp of Jack Parsons' story before this recent dive into his work, and so now I'm not sure how much I believe this whole narrative.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I think that the elixir of eternal life is them living on in people's minds, like parasites in their minds, like a Cthulhu-esque type thing, forever.", "author": "Juan Ayala", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/c975ca54-711c-4695-b561-cffc1c0b10d2/JUAN-AYALA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I feel like if this guy had made some serious efforts to look within instead of always looking without, his life could have been different.", "author": "Kayleigh Berkana", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/5c923247-58f8-42f0-a64e-59357e5336f4/KAYLEIGH-BERKANA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
